messages:
marta: Ran a full nsys + perfetto profile on the 8xA100 cluster with the latest kernel-selector change. Seeing periodic pipeline bubbles aligned with NCCL all-reduce spikes and a KV-cache handshake that looks suspiciously synchronous.

raj: Can you paste the trace links + nsys cmd?

marta: nsys: `nsys profile --trace=cuda,nvtx,nccl --output=run_1781234567.qdrep --sample=none --force true --duration=120`
perfetto: link in the bucket s3://redwood-traces/eng-runtime/1781234567/perfetto.html (uploaded). qdrep also at s3://redwood-traces/eng-runtime/1781234567/nsys.qdrep

lucy: Quick summary from the nsys summary: matmul_128x128 ~= 42% GPU time, fused_attention_fwd ~= 21%, kernel_launch_overhead ~= 6%, nccl_allreduce ~= 11%. Top hotspot is matmul_128x128 but there are thousands of very short launches (0.02-0.06ms) that dominate overhead.

raj: So small matmuls + lots of all-reduce calls => poor overlap. Does the NCCL timeline show the all-reduce aligning with TP boundaries?

marta: Yes — each token generation step does: (1) KV write, (2) small metadata memcpy to host, (3) call that ends up causing an NCCL group/sync for a tiny tensor. That allreduce is not being coalesced and it stalls the pipeline.

lucy: Hypothesis: batching heuristic emits microbatches of size 1 frequently, which produces tiny matmuls and forces frequent nccl calls. Two immediate mitigations: aggregate microbatches (hold for a few ms) or coalesce NCCL ops (grouping).

marta: I tried toggling BATCH_MAX_WAIT_MS=5ms on a replica — tail latency improves ~18% for single-token streams, but median increases slightly for bursty traffic. Preliminary trace attached.

perf-bot: nsys summary attached: GPU kernel breakdown (top 4): [matmul_128x128: 41.7%], [fused_attention_fwd: 21.3%], [nccl_allreduce: 11.2%], [kernel_launch: 6.0%]. Observed ~1200 allreduce bursts over 2 minute run; avg allreduce duration 0.9ms, p95 1.8ms. Many matmuls are 0.03-0.08ms.

raj: Two code hypotheses: (A) KV handshake does an unnecessary blocking host sync; (B) runtime calls ncclGroupEnd per micro-op instead of coalescing across micro-ops. Either would cause the pattern you're seeing.

marta: I instrumented NVTX scopes — confirmed: we do a `cudaMemcpy` for the KV metadata on the hot path, followed by a small NCCL op. That memcpy is on host-synchronous memory buffer.

lucy: Low-effort fixes to try: 1) switch metadata copies to async+pinned buffer; 2) defer the KV handshakes until after we accumulate microbatch; 3) group NCCL calls (ncclGroupStart/End around multiple ops). All carry risk — grouping NCCL might change p2p patterns.

raj: Also consider kernel selector rule: prefer slightly larger-tile matmul that reduces number of launches when shapes are tiny. Might reduce launch overhead even if single-kernel latency increases a bit. But we must run perf regression tests.

marta: Reproducer script: gen_bench.py --seq-len 64 --streaming --microbatch=1,2,4 --tp=8 --profile=nsys. Uploaded to s3://redwood-traces/eng-runtime/1781234567/gen_bench.py

lucy: I'll add a CI perf regression test that runs batch sizes [1,2,4] and compares tail latency before/after kernel-selector changes. Keep the baseline trace for comparison.

perf-bot: Tagged traces: s3://redwood-traces/eng-runtime/1781234567/nsys.qdrep and https://perfetto.app/trace/abc123 (placeholder).

raj: I can run an A/B on dev-rig tonight: (A) defer KV handshake; (B) keep handshake but enable microbatch aggregation. Will post traces.

marta: I opened an issue: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/issues/512 (linked the nsys + perfetto artifacts). Will add small change to runtime to use pinned async copy for KV metadata in a PR and run nsys.

lucy: If async copy + deferred handshake removes the periodic NCCL spikes we should see ~20-30% tail drop for single-token streams. Also we need to be careful about regressions on medium batch sizes — add the perf-ci guard.

raj: One more note: check whether NCCL tunables (NCCL_BUFFSIZE, NCCL_COLLNET_ENABLE, etc.) affect behavior on our TP config. Some options can reduce latency for many small ops.

marta: Good call. I'll test NCCL_BUFFSIZE=16384 and also try NCCL_ASYNC_ERROR_HANDLING=1 for stability.

lucy: OK action items: marta -> PR for pinned+async memcpy + run nsys; raj -> A/B microbatch vs handshake defer on dev rig and upload traces; lucy -> add perf regression job and kernel-selector test. Regroup tomorrow with traces. :white_check_mark:
